subject: th-cont
title: TH.CONT.------TRS.
description: Diagram in R(AS)CM(II)-25 — the section on performance-space culture-function and the unequal distribution of performance outlets. The prose immediately above identifies the structural ground: 'the performance of classical music is not about economics as such — because whatever has to be done to keep the music will be done... The reality of any form of creative music is related to whether or not that form can have the possibility of performance — and the focus realness of creative music must also be viewed with this in mind.' The crossing diagrams how thrust-continuance structurally meets transition when performance-possibility is the working partner: TH-CONT (thrust continuance — the form's actual forward motion) crossed with TRS (transition). TH-CONT sits on the left with the subject-arrow; its main line runs right to TRS, passing through C-INFO (composite information), which sits on the line at top-center. From C-INFO's point a line drops down-right and bends to PROJ-CONT (projectional continuance); T-CONT hangs at lower-left from that line, and IST-F (isolated focus) at the bottom-right is joined to T-CONT's line by a *dashed* line. Structural argument: when thrust-continuance is crossed with transition, the main line TH-CONT → C-INFO → TRS is the *culture-function route* — thrust-continuance routes through composite-information into transition only when composite-information actually holds the main line. The performing spaces the prose says 'are conceived with respect to the perpetuation of what is considered "culture"' are structurally the culture-function that selectively holds the main line through C-INFO — for classical, against creative.
